mechanism_claims.claim_text: The peptides perturb the E. coli LPS outer membrane in cell-based zeta-potential and NPN fluorescence assays.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure curves are used qualitatively; no exact plotted zeta/NPN point values are asserted in this artifact.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: PM15, PM15Y and PM15A for LPS ITC; PM15 and PM15Y for NMR structures
mechanism_claims.claim_text: The peptides bind LPS with submicromolar Kd values and PM15/PM15Y adopt beta-hairpin structures in LPS micelles.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The PM15/LPS docking model is treated as supportive computational context, not as standalone direct mechanism proof.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: PM15 and PM15Y bind E. coli LptAm by ITC, supporting a target-interaction component of the proposed LPS-transport mode of action.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper infers possible LPS transport inhibition from binding; it does not directly assay LPS transport blockade in this study.
